videos.desc:
Benedict Arnold's Top 3 Legendary Tactical Moves | The Man Who Turned the Tide at Saratoga
By 1777 the Revolution was going badly: the British held New York and Philadelphia, and a second 
British army came down from Canada. At Saratoga, on the Hudson, about six thousand of its soldiers 
laid down their arms, and the victory brought France into the war. The man who broke the British 
line that day had no command at all. Three years later his name would become another word for 
traitor. This is what he did before that.

Despite being heavily outnumbered and facing a dug-in enemy that knew they were coming, the battalion executed a series of maneuvers that secured a decisive victory. This analysis covers the leadership of Major Chris Keeble and the risks taken during the engagement in the Falklands War.
